Flat, at size

An outset adds to a stroke exactly what it takes from the gap beside it. That is why the diamond could never just be thickened: its white facets were already the tightest thing in the lockup. Weight alone eats them; size alone keeps the ratio and buys nothing; the two together can hold any stroke at any facet. The figures under the controls are that arithmetic — stroke = size × 0.98 + 2 × weight, facet = size × 2.07 − 2 × weight — and running the line above re-measures the built artwork rather than predicting it — which matters past about +0.30 of diamond weight, where the two stop agreeing. The arithmetic keeps promising stroke; the measurement says the strokes have stopped getting thicker and only the facets are still closing. At +0.50 it predicts 1.98 and the built artwork measures 1.63, for a facet down at 1.12.
